stem: A team wants to block one group from reading a table that lives in a Unity Catalog schema, and someone proposes the DENY statement. The reviewer asks whether it is available for an object governed this way.

option_texts.A: Yes, the statement works on any securable and takes precedence over a grant
option_texts.B: No, the statement is not supported by Unity Catalog and covers hive_metastore only
option_texts.C: Yes, but only once the group's existing grants have been revoked first
option_texts.D: No, because denying is expressed by revoking the grant in every catalog

drill_answer_short: DENY is not supported by Unity Catalog; the statement applies only to the hive_metastore catalog and its objects
decision_hinge: The DENY statement denies a privilege on a securable object to a principal, but this function is not supported by Unity Catalog and the statement applies only to the hive_metastore catalog and its objects.

eliminated_by.C: block one group from reading a table that lives in a Unity Catalog schema
eliminated_by.D: The reviewer asks whether it is available for an object governed this way

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - precedence over a grant is real behaviour, but only in the hive_metastore catalog
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - revoking first does not make the statement available on this catalog
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - revoke undoes a deny, it is not how a deny is expressed

stem: A pipeline declares a streaming table with one expectation named valid_customer_age. A downstream report still shows ages above 120, so invalid records are clearly reaching the target. The pipeline must keep running while invalid records stop reaching the target, and the team needs to know why the current declaration retains them. Nothing else in the pipeline filters rows.

option_texts.A: Rewrite the clause as EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE so an invalid record stops the update
option_texts.B: Rewrite the query to filter the rows in SQL, because expectations cannot remove records from the target
option_texts.C: Rewrite the clause as EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION DROP ROW, because a bare EXPECT keeps invalid records
option_texts.D: Rewrite the expectation with a second constraint name, because one name per dataset only warns

drill_answer_short: warn is the default action, so a bare EXPECT still writes invalid records to the target; ON VIOLATION DROP ROW drops them
decision_hinge: warn is the default action and invalid records are written to the target; EXPECT ... ON VIOLATION DROP ROW means invalid records are dropped before data is written to the target.

plausible_options.A: invalid records stop reaching the target

eliminated_by.B: the team needs to know why the current declaration retains them
eliminated_by.D: A downstream report still shows ages above 120

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - FAIL UPDATE stops the update instead of letting the pipeline keep running
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - expectations can drop invalid records, so a hand-written SQL filter is not the fix
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the expectation name is an identifier and never controls the action on invalid records

stem: A job runs several notebook tasks that all need the same processing_region value, and the operator wants to set it once when starting a run rather than editing each step. The value should reach every step that takes key-value input. No step may hard-code it.

option_texts.A: Define it as a job parameter, a key-value pair pushed down to tasks
option_texts.B: Define it as a task parameter on each step, a key-value pair supplied per task
option_texts.C: Define it as a cluster environment variable, which every notebook on that cluster reads
option_texts.D: Define it in a shared notebook that each step imports before it does any work

drill_answer_short: Job parameters are key-value pairs defined at job level and pushed down to tasks
decision_hinge: A job parameter is a key-value pair defined at the job level and pushed down to tasks, while a task parameter is a key-value pair or JSON array defined at the task level.

plausible_options.B: the operator wants to set it once when starting a run rather than editing each step

eliminated_by.C: several notebook tasks that all need the same processing_region value
eliminated_by.D: The value should reach every step that takes key-value input

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - task parameters are real, but they are set per task, which is the editing being avoided
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - an environment variable is a compute setting and is not part of the run request
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - a shared notebook carries code, not a per-run value

stem: A job is scheduled every fifteen minutes, but one afternoon a run takes almost an hour. The team reviews the history afterwards and has to account for what became of the triggers that fired while the long run was still going. No concurrency limit was raised.

option_texts.A: They were skipped, because only one run of a job may be active
option_texts.B: They were queued and replayed in order once the long run finally finished
option_texts.C: They started in parallel, because a schedule is independent of any run in flight
option_texts.D: They failed and were recorded as errors against the schedule that produced them

drill_answer_short: By default only one run of a job is active at a time, and runs from most trigger types are skipped beyond that limit
decision_hinge: By default only a single run of a job can be active at a time, and runs from most trigger types are skipped when they exceed the configured max concurrency for a job.

plausible_options.B: account for what became of the triggers that fired while the long run was still going

eliminated_by.C: A job is scheduled every fifteen minutes
eliminated_by.D: The team reviews the history afterwards

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - job completion triggers do retain a ready completion, but a schedule does not queue
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - concurrency is capped at one run unless the limit is raised
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a skipped trigger is not recorded as a failure
